4. The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner, during the course of the arguments referred to the suicide note which was stated to be written by the deceased and argued that in the suicide note, the deceased has mentioned only about the unhealthy relationship with the petitioner and it appeared that she was not happy with her relationship with the petitioner.

It is also reflected from the suicide note that the father of the petitioner namely, Mr. Narender Singh had demanded Rs.6,00,000/- as he had spent about Rs. 12,00,000/- on the MBA course of the petitioner.
The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner further argued that these are only vague allegations without any specific allegation of dowry demand in the suicide note.
The father and the brother of the deceased have already been examined-in-chief before the trial court.
In these circumstances, the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner prayed that the bail application be allowed and the petitioner be admitted to bail.
5. The bail application is opposed by the counsel for the respondent/State.

He further argued that the father of the petitioner had demanded Rs. 6,00,000/- from the family of the deceased as he allegedly had spent Rs. 12,00,000/- on the MBA course of the petitioner.

He further argued that the father and the brother of the deceased are examined-in-chief before the trial court and the cross-examination is fixed for 05.12.2023.
6.

The counsel for the complainant also stated that the sister of the petitioner was granted anticipatory bail as she had a one-year old child and the father of the petitioner was granted bail on manipulated and fabricated medical documents pertaining to his wife.
The allegations against the petitioner are serious in nature and he was responsible for the untimely death of the deceased.
The deceased had died within one year of marriage under unnatural circumstances because of dowry demand.
It is prayed that the present bail application be dismissed.
7. The petitioner is stated to be in judicial custody since 12.06.2021.
The investigation has already been completed.
The trial is pending, wherein the father and the brother of the deceased have already been examined-in-chief.
The perusal of the suicide note, at this stage, reflects that the deceased was not happy with the behaviour and conduct of the petitioner towards her.
The allegations pertaining to the dowry demand are confined to Rs. 6,00,000/- as the father of the petitioner is stated to have spent Rs. 12,00,000/- on the MBA course of the petitioner.
There is no possibility of the petitioner to flee away or to avoid the trial.
